column3: The Hebrew repeats Shechem; BSB uses “there” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats Egypt and Jeroboam where BSB uses pronouns.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here; BSB explicitly names Rehoboam.
The Hebrew describes the elders as standing before Solomon; BSB interprets this as serving him.
The Hebrew coordinates pleasing them and speaking good words to them; BSB makes speaking kindly the means of pleasing them.
The Hebrew describes the young men as standing before him; BSB describes them as serving him.
The Hebrew says “my little one” and “my father’s loins”; BSB specifies “my little finger” and says “waist.”
The Hebrew says they came on the third day; BSB initially says “after three days.”
The Hebrew begins the speech with “I will make your yoke heavy”; BSB begins with “My father made your yoke heavy.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly say Israel saw this. It states there is no inheritance in Jesse’s son, where BSB asks a question. The final movement is to their tents; BSB says they went home.
The Hebrew describes Rehoboam hastening to mount his chariot in order to flee; BSB explicitly says he escaped.
